q: Define the “Law of Supply” and explain it with the help of a schedule and curve?
a: Answers: Law of Supply: "Other things remaining the same, as the price of a commodity rises, its supply is extended, and as the price falls, its supply is contracted." Explanation: The Law of Supply is just the opposite of the Law of Demand. i.e, when the price increases, the supply also increases and the supply decreases with the fall in price. It means the supply has a functional relationship with price because the quantity offered for sale varies directly with the price i.e. the higher the price, the larger the supply, and vice versa. Supply Schedule: Explanation of the supply schedule: According to the given schedule (Table), when the price is the highest i.e. Rs. 30 per K.g., the suppliers or sellers are willing 10 sales a large quantity of 3,000 K.g. of a particular commodity but as price falls, continuously, i.e. Rs. 25, 20, 15 and Rs. 10, the supply also falls accordingly i.e. 2,500 Kg., to 2,000, 1,500 and 1,000 K.g. It means as the price falls, the supply contracts and if the price rises the supply extends. The supply schedule proves the accuracy of the Law of Supply that "other things remaining the same, when the price of a particular commodity falls in the market, less quantity of it is offered for sale; and with a rise in price more quantity is offered for sale." It means that supply has a functional relationship with price. Supply Curve: Explanation of Supply Curve: The price of the commodity is mentioned on the axis O.Y. and the quantity supplied is shown on axis O.X. S.S' is the supply curve. The curve explains the Law of Supply in the way that at the price of Rs.10, the supply is 1000 K.g., mentioned on the line S.S'. From O.to A. i.e. O. A when the price rises to Rs.15 the supply increases to 1500 K.g. i.e. OB. Then with the rise in Price to Rs.20, 25, and Rs.30; the supply also increases to 2,000, 2,500, and 3,000 K.g. Thus the Supply Curve rises high from 0.A. to O.B., 0.C., OD and up to O.E. The curve represents the Law of Demand that the supply increases with an increase in price and it falls with a fall in price.

q: Write down the assumptions law of Supply and narrate the factors affecting Supply?
a: Answers: Assumptions of the Law of Supply: There are certain conditions to prove the accuracy of the Law of Supply. These conditions are called "Assumptions". They are as follows: Change in cost of production: When there is any change in the cost of production, there is a change in price also in this condition the supply is inversely affected and there is the possibility of no increase or decrease in supply. Change in techniques of production: Sometimes the new techniques of production lessen the cost of production. In this case, the supply may Increase without any rise in price; which may cause the failure of the law. Change in the prices of machines and raw materials: Machines and raw materials are basic requirements of production. They play a very important role to change the cost of production. When there is a rise in their prices, there is a rise in the selling price of a commodity. In this case, a rise in price will not be followed by a rise in supply and the law will not hold good. Factors Affecting Supply: The causes of changes in supply are called the factors affecting supply in Economics. They are as under Time Factor: Supply of a particular commodity is relevant to its period of production. The supply can be increased only when the required commodity is produced in a short period. On the other hand, certain goods require a long period to be produced and cannot be supplied instantly e.g, wheat, rice, fruits, machines, motor cars, etc. In this case, their supply cannot be increased and will not be affected by any change in price.
